issues.issue: The proviso lets the Borrower and a counterparty substitute Minnesota or other governing law into the Consent and Agreement "without the consent of the Required Lenders or the Security Agent being required", with no limit on which laws qualify. What the Secured Parties have agreed to accept is therefore open-ended.

"The power to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of a Person ... by contract or otherwise" has no percentage benchmark, so control is a matter of judgment in every case. The catch-all "or otherwise" widens it further.

After the specifics "cash, inventory and accounts receivable", the catch-all "other assets that are due, or likely to be converted into cash, sold, exchanged, or expensed in the normal course of business, within one (1) year" turns on the vague test "likely to be". Its reach against the enumerated items is genuinely uncertain.

"Any matters disclosed in the Confidential Information Material" incorporates an entire information memorandum and data site without identifying what counts as a disclosed matter. The breadth of the carve-out from representations is left at large.
"Any items treated as exceptional or extraordinary items" gives no standard for who so treats them or by what criteria. The add-back is therefore capable of materially different computations.

The Commercial Operations Date definition requires certification by the "Lenders' Engineering Consultant", a label that does not match this defined term. Whether Noramco acting under this definition is the same certifier is left open.

"Relating in any way to the environment" coupled with "notices or binding agreements" as sources of law makes the category of Environmental Laws very hard to bound. The width of "in any way" is the contestable point.

The catch-all "any other material contract entered into by the Borrower with respect to any engineering, procurement or construction services" follows four named contracts, and "material" is undefined. Whether a given supply or services contract is an EPC Contract is left to argument.

The Borrower must deposit "all Cash and receivables arising out of any contracts of the Borrower with any Person or payments otherwise received by Borrower", a sweep of literally every receipt with no carve-out for operating funds. How far that obligation actually reaches is a live question.

Everything deposited is said to be "applied in accordance with the Cash Sweep Mechanism", yet Section 2.05 requires Loans to be funded into the same Escrow Account and then "made available to the Borrower" for Project costs. The two directions for the same account cannot both be applied literally.

The definition ends by preserving "any successor collateral agent appointed pursuant to the Collateral Account Agreement", although the office being defined is escrow agent and account bank and the Agreement separately appoints a Security Agent. The mismatched label leaves the succession mechanism uncertain.

The definition omits the operative verb — "'Existing Credit Agreement' the Credit Agreement dated September 22, 2010" — so it is a sentence fragment. The omission is trivial to cure but is a mechanical defect on the face of the text.

The numerator is limited to assets over which the Secured Parties hold a first priority interest "subject only to Permitted Liens thereon", but the Agreement defines "Permitted Encumbrances", not "Permitted Liens". The undefined term makes the FACR calculation contestable.

Financial Closure requires Total Commitments of US$530,000,000, but the Total Commitment definition fixes US$250,000,000 unless Accession Agreements are entered into, and Section 2.02(b) makes Tranche B available only after Financial Closure. Whether Tranche B can ever be drawn absent accession is a genuine question.

The long enumerated list of events closes with "or other similar acts beyond the reasonable control of the Borrower", a classic ejusdem generis catch-all whose reach against the specifics is uncertain. "Similar" to which of acts of God, strikes, weather or machinery breakage is not stated.

"A jurisdiction other than that in which the Borrower is located" turns on the undefined notion of where a borrower is "located", and the final sentence contemplates a Borrower located in more than one jurisdiction. The test for Foreign Lender status is therefore not self-applying.

"And related proceedings thereto that may be filed elsewhere in Federal or state court" extends the defined litigation to unidentified future proceedings without any test of relatedness. What falls inside the Great Lakes Litigation, and hence inside the disclosed matters, is left open.
